issue.title: bash gate: `rm -rf x 2>/dev/null` parses the redirect as delete targets, hits the no-escape protected-path tier

steps: Run exactly this bash command and report the result: cd /tmp && rm -rf nonexistent-test-dir-xyz 2>/dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
expected: The only delete operand resolves to /tmp/nonexistent-test-dir-xyz; the redirect is not a delete target.
defect: The gate treats the descriptor 2 and /dev/null as deletion operands and may resolve the relative target against HOME instead of the cd directory.
Root cause: Redirect syntax is not removed from the operand list before destructive-target assessment, and command-local cd state is not propagated into relative-path resolution. Commit 9b2480bf is a related parser fix on a diverged history, so ancestry alone cannot establish whether current pin has the semantic fix.

_meta.notes: The non-existent throwaway path is verbatim from the issue. No command is executed while preparing this file. Require the refusal to identify /dev/null as a delete target, not an ordinary permitted approval request.
_meta.version_installation_validation: not_executed; historical launch and dependency compatibility must be checked before running
